title.value: The Invasion of Ukraine Viewed through TikTok: A Dataset
title.justification: The title accurately represents the content of the paper, which explores how TikTok portrays the invasion of Ukraine through data analysis.
title.quote: "The Invasion of Ukraine Viewed through TikTok: A Dataset"

extractions.description: The paper presents a dataset of TikTok video descriptions, comments, and user statistics centered around the invasion of Ukraine in 2022. The dataset aims to explore the role of TikTok in shaping social and political dynamics concerning the invasion. The study also analyses language and interaction dynamics and assesses bot detection on TikTok. Furthermore, the dataset is open-sourced to enable further research into these dynamics.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper primarily focuses on social media dynamics related to a geopolitical event rather than addressing climate or ecologically-related sustainable development issues.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Despite the appearance of a role in shaping how the war is seen around the world, little is concretely known about the nature and extent of this influence.

primary_category.justification: The paper does not address any climate or ecologically-related sustainable development issues. It is centered on social media analysis concerning the Ukraine invasion.
primary_category.quote: Given this, we seek to investigate...the relationship between TikTok and the social communications and interactions surrounding the invasion of Ukraine.

secondary_categories.justification: There are no secondary themes related to climate or ecological sustainability mentioned in the paper.
secondary_categories.quote: We present a dataset of video descriptions, comments, and user statistics, from the social media platform TikTok, centred around the invasion of Ukraine in 2022, an event that launched TikTok into the geopolitical arena.

primary_sub_category.justification: No sub-category related to climate or ecological sustainability can be identified in the paper.
primary_sub_category.quote: ...an initial investigation of language and social interaction dynamics, alongside an evaluation of bot detection on the platform.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: There are no secondary sub-categories applicable as the paper does not engage with climate or ecological themes.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: To create the dataset, we identified hashtags and keywords explicitly related to the conflict to collect a core set of videos (or “TikToks”).

applications.justification: The paper is not related to any climate or ecological applications but rather to social interaction on TikTok related to the Ukraine invasion.
applications.quote: We present a dataset of video descriptions, comments, and user statistics, from the social media platform TikTok, centred around the invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

new_primary_category.justification: The existing categories cover climate and ecological sustainability which are not applicable to this paper.
new_primary_category.quote: To this end, we provide a mass-scale language and interaction dataset for further research into these processes.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The existing sub-categories do not apply to this paper as it is unrelated to climate or ecological concerns.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: Quantitative research as a field has generally focused on Twitter and Facebook so far...there is a severe gap in our understanding of other social media platforms.
